what_its_for: Praziquantel is used to treat infections caused by certain parasitic worms, including tapeworms (such as beef, pork, and fish tapeworms) and schistosomiasis (a disease caused by blood flukes). It works by paralyzing and killing the worms so your body can get rid of them.
how_to_take: Take praziquantel by mouth with a full glass of water. Swallow the tablets whole — do not chew them because they taste very bitter and may cause gagging or vomiting. Take each dose with food or shortly after a meal to help reduce stomach upset. If your doctor prescribes more than one dose per day, space the doses evenly throughout the day (usually 4 to 6 hours apart).
dosing: Your doctor will decide the exact dose and number of doses based on the type of infection you have and your body weight. Some infections are treated with a single dose, while others may require multiple doses taken in one day or over a few days. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Contact your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store praziquantel tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the medication away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the packaging.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice while taking praziquantel, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be fully alert on the day of treatment and the day after, because praziquantel can cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol during treatment as it may worsen dizziness and nausea. Do not take rifampin (a common antibiotic) within 4 weeks of your praziquantel dose, as it can make praziquantel much less effective.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe stomach pain, seizures, vision changes, confusion, severe headache, skin rash or hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you have ongoing nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or if your symptoms do not improve after completing treatment. Let your doctor know if you have a history of liver disease or epilepsy before starting this medication.
when_it_works: Praziquantel starts working quickly — it begins killing the worms within hours of taking the dose. Most people complete treatment within one day for many types of infections. Your doctor may order a follow-up stool test or blood test a few weeks after treatment to confirm the infection has cleared. You may not notice obvious changes in how you feel right away, but the worms will be eliminated from your body over the days following treatment.
special_populations: Children: Praziquantel can be used in children, but dosing is based on body weight. The tablets are very bitter, so young children may have difficulty swallowing them whole. Talk to your doctor about the best way to give this medication to a child. Pregnant Women: Praziquantel is generally not recommended during the first trimester of pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before taking this medication. Breastfeeding Mothers: Small amounts of praziquantel pass into breast milk. It is recommended to avoid breastfeeding on the day of treatment and for 72 hours (3 days) afterward. During this time, pump and discard your breast milk to maintain your milk supply, then resume breastfeeding after 3 days. Older Adults and People with Liver Disease: Use this medication with caution if you have liver problems, as it is processed through the liver. Your doctor may monitor you more closely or adjust your dose.
